compositions.description: Name/title card sliding in from the bottom-left. Use when introducing a person, naming a claim's source, or opening a section.

variables.label: Primary line (e.g. a name or claim)
Secondary line (e.g. a title or context), can be empty

compositions.description: A big number with a short label, scale-punched into center screen. Use when the speaker states a specific statistic, percentage, or dollar figure worth emphasizing.

variables.label: What the stat measures, can be empty

compositions.description: A short quoted line in large centered text. Use for one punchy, quotable sentence the speaker just said -- not a paraphrase, the actual words.

variables.label: The quoted line, kept short (under ~10 words)

compositions.description: One or two words scale-punched onto the screen for emphasis. Use for a single high-impact word or short phrase (e.g. 'NEVER', 'FREE', 'the #1 mistake'). Costs very little screen time -- fine to use more than once per clip if the moments are far enough apart.

variables.label: The word or short phrase to emphasize

compositions.description: A decorative border treatment around the whole frame with an optional corner label. Use sparingly -- once per clip at most -- to bookend an intro or signal a segment change.

variables.label: A short corner label (e.g. a section name), can be empty

compositions.description: A small 'N / total' step indicator with dots, bottom-center. Use when the speaker is visibly walking through an enumerated list or numbered steps.

variables.label: Current step number, as a string (e.g. '2')
Total step count, as a string (e.g. '3')
